title: Mycelial / Artificial Cortex: distributed tokens, waves, and modal computational tissue
summary: This pass restores a June side-branch that turns out to be an important ancestor of the current computational-matter line. TheMycelialCortex treated sparse spikes as tokens moving between independently organized resident substrates, while ArtificialCortex made the substrate explicitly spatial and spectral: coupled oscillatory fields, traveling waves, slow/fast bands, and a frequency axis as part of the computational state. Neither establishes a biological cortex. What survives into the later FANMC / operator-composition work is the architectural move away from 'a neuron as a weighted scalar unit' toward matter with resident dynamics that must be addressed through sparse external events.

nodes.claim: Builds a distributed geometric-neuron substrate whose local memories grow, consolidate and communicate across machines using sparse spike/token messages rather than shared weights.
nodes.survived: The interface idea is durable: a small sparse event can communicate with a much richer resident machine, and two peers can organize the same token stream into different internal structures. The repo also makes growth, fatigue and order-sensitive traffic explicit state variables.
nodes.killed: The live system fragmented memories into many redundant nodes, and temporal order did not federate in the demonstrated relay. Federation of sparse tokens is not evidence of distributed cognition or a biological mycelial mechanism.

nodes.claim: Couples time-holding / coincidence-sensitive units into spatial oscillatory fields with traveling waves, interference, slow-fast coupling and a stacked spatial-by-frequency representation.
nodes.survived: A field can be treated as resident computational matter whose useful coordinates include space, frequency and phase; slow state can gate faster dynamics; and computation can be read from wave/interference structure rather than only from trained feedforward weights. The archived `the_whorl/whorl_field.py` is the concrete spiral branch: circular/tangential coupling bias pins a spiral core, and that exact file is also preserved in the later GeometricNeuron_V20 curation.
nodes.killed: The mechanisms are established dynamical-systems ingredients assembled synthetically, not a derivation of cortex. The grid symmetry and several clocks are supplied by construction, the energy quantity is a proxy, and the repo does not establish advantage over ordinary learned systems.

edges.why: TheMycelialCortex explicitly states that it is built on the Geometric Neuron / GAIT / Ephaptic Spiking Field series.
TheMycelialCortex README explicitly says it uses PerceptionLab and is presented as a PerceptionLab substrate.
ArtificialCortex explicitly names the Mycelial Cortex line in its lineage and reuses the same resident-dynamics / sparse-event framing at field scale.
ArtificialCortex explicitly states that it is built on the geometric-neuron / Mycelial Cortex line.

motifs.title: Resident computational matter can be addressed in space, frequency and sparse events
motifs.description: TheMycelialCortex makes sparse events/tokens the communication interface to independently organized resident machines. ArtificialCortex turns the resident machine into spatial oscillatory tissue with frequency and phase coordinates. InformationFlow later makes WHERE/WHICH/SIGN addressing explicit, and FrequencyAddressedNonlinearModalCell turns the same idea into a black-box stimulation language with strong attackers. The recurring object is not a biological cortex claim but a programmable substrate whose internal dynamics are richer than the event used to address them.
